prompt:
Is a thread in crunch ready to run but never getting to? Which one, and why?

Begin your answer with exactly one line: "Verdict: yes", "Verdict: no", or "Verdict: cannot tell from this trace". Then answer the question.
answer:
Verdict: no

## CPU scheduling

The thread is **calc-4 (TID 635007, in crunch)**. Over the full trace window (0–30,613.940 ms), it spent 15.124 ms waiting for a CPU; 3 waits lasted at least 1 ms, and none lasted 10 ms. Its longest wait after being woken was 1.674 ms, at offset 1,395.955 ms. In that interval, it was runnable on CPU 8 while TID 2730032 (codium) occupied that CPU.

So calc-4 did experience a measurable scheduling delay, but the total was modest and the longest runnable wait was short; the findings do not show that it was materially held back or “never” got to run. A runnable thread is ready to execute but not currently running on a CPU [1].

## Where its time went

Over the same window, calc-4 was blocked for 87.4% of its alive time, mostly in futex waits; 300 waits ended with a wake-up from crunch’s main thread, typically consistent with a worker waiting for new work. It ran in user mode for 10.3%.

### All sources used:
1) Runnable time and CPU contention - https://archive.eclipse.org/tracecompass/doc/stable/org.eclipse.tracecompass.doc.user/LTTng-Kernel-Analysis.html
